articles.title_original: Yemeni military says it has 'secured' Red Sea waterway
articles.title_zh: Yemeni military says it has 'secured' Red Sea waterway
facts_zh:
Yemeni military says it has 'secured' Red Sea waterway
- Published
Yemeni pro-government forces backed by Saudi Arabia say they have "secured" the Bab al-Mandab Strait at the southern end of the Red Sea, at the start of a major offensive against the Iran-backed Houthi movement.

The Yemeni military also said in a statement that National Shield, Giants Brigades and Tihama Resistance forces had captured the Red Sea city of Mokha on Monday afternoon with the help of Saudi air strikes.
But in conflicting reports, unnamed Yemeni government and military sources told news agencies Reuters and AFP that the forces have only reached the city's outskirts.

all_titles.en: Yemeni military says it has 'secured' Red Sea waterway

articles.title_zh: Trump says 'threat' led US to pull bombers from RAF Fairford
facts_zh:
Trump says 'threat' led US to pull bombers from RAF Fairford
- Published
President Donald Trump has said the US moved its bombers out of RAF Fairford because of "some threats" to the base.
The Pentagon confirmed on Sunday it had removed its bombers - thought to be about a dozen B-1s - from the base back to their home stations in America.
Speaking to reporters as he departed for Nebraska on Monday, Trump said the US had known of a "threat", which led them to move the bombers.

articles.title_original: US 'watching closely' after plague researcher dies in Russia
articles.title_zh: US 'watching closely' after plague researcher dies in Russia
facts_zh:
US 'watching closely' after plague researcher dies in Russia
- Published
President Donald Trump says the US is looking "very strongly" at the case of a Russian lab technician who died at a plague research centre in Siberia.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was watching closely amid concerns the incident could lead to the spread of pneumonic plague, but there was no cause for alarm.
Announcing the cause of death as "pneumonia of undetermined etiology", Irkutsk's governor said "no micro-organisms" linked to the woman's work had been found "in her biological samples".

all_titles.en: US 'watching closely' after plague researcher dies in Russia

articles.title_original: Flávio Bolsonaro poised to win Brazilian presidency after shock first-round victory
articles.title_zh: Flávio Bolsonaro poised to win Brazilian presidency after shock first-round victory
facts_zh: Progressive voters and supporters of incumbent president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva left reeling after far-right surge Flávio Bolsonaro is in pole position to win Brazil’s presidential election, after a far-right tsunami propelled him to a shock first-round victory over the incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, leaving progressive voters reeling.

The 45-year-old rightwing candidate received 56.1m votes to Lula’s 53.8m – 47.03% to 45.16% – meaning the 80-year-old leftwinger has a mountain to climb if he is to bounce back in the second round on 25 October.
Never, since the return of democracy to Brazil in 1985, has the first-round runner-up managed to turn the game around and win the second ballot.

all_titles.en: Flávio Bolsonaro poised to win Brazilian presidency after shock first-round victory

articles.title_zh: Spain PM pins hopes on housing crisis to help win snap election
facts_zh:
Spain PM pins hopes on housing crisis to help win snap election
- Published
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's decision to call a snap election for 29 November came on the back of a parliamentary defeat.

On Friday, the raft of measures he had presented to congress aimed at improving conditions for tenants and trying to address the problem of soaring rentals was narrowly rejected, as parties on the right voted against them.
That parliamentary result confirmed that Sánchez's left-wing coalition no longer commanded a majority.

all_titles.en: Spain PM pins hopes on housing crisis to help win snap election

articles.title_zh: Pentagon stops using Anthropic AI tools after blacklisting company, BBC told
facts_zh:
Pentagon stops using Anthropic AI tools after blacklisting company, BBC told
- Published
The US Department of Defence is no longer using Anthropic's AI tools, an official has told the BBC, months after it designated the company a supply chain risk on national security grounds.
The Pentagon "has ceased the use of Anthropic products", the department official said in a statement on Monday.
Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth labelled Anthropic a supply chain risk in February, and announced that the Pentagon would stop using it by late August.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has condemned a "horrific" Russian attack on a vessel carrying corn in the Black Sea.

Eleven crew members - nationals of Azerbaijan and India - have been rescued.
